title: WPPIL/9/2017 of Dr. Pramod Nainwal Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No.9 of 2017
Dr. Pramod Nainwal
 .....Petitioner
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & Ors.
 .......Respondents
Ms. Shivangi Gangwar, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Pradeep Joshi, Standing Counsel for the State.
Dated: 24.04.2017
Coram: Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Hon'ble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.

V.K. Bist, J. (Oral)
Petitioner has approached this Court seeking
the following reliefs:
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus directing the
respondents to prohibit sale and purchase of
liquor in the entire State of Uttarakhand.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus directing the
respondents to prepare a master plan for
making strong boundaries (through strong
iron cables) between the forest areas and the
villages of the hilly regions of the State so that
the agriculture and human life of these
villages can be prevented from wild animals.
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondents to provide adequate facilities
(including funds and infrastructure) to the

2
farmers of the hilly regions of State and to
establish small scale industries in the hilly
regions such as plywood factories (65% of the
State is forest area) and other wooden based
small industries so that migration be
prevented from these village/hilly regions."
2. Petitioner claims himself to be a public
spirited person and an Organizer of 'Palayan Roko,
Nasha Hatao, Pahar Bachao' Samiti Bhikiyasain District
Almora. According to the petitioner, almost most part of
the State of Uttarakhand is hilly area where the source
of employment is so meager and the population of village
is dependent on their small agriculture. The State
Government has failed to provide adequate facilities and
protection to these small farmers and has also failed to
make serious efforts in promoting self employment and
small scale industries in hilly terrain of the State and
due to this inaction on the part of the State, most of the
population of hilly terrain is being compelled to migrate
to other States or plain area of their State for their
livelihood. The State Government has almost failed to
prevent this migration due to which the State is suffering
severe losses. The example of migration can be examined
from Village Chaubatakhal District Pauri Garhwal where
almost every person of the village has been migrated and
there the population has become almost Nil and similar
situation will arise soon in other villages of the State if
the State fails to make a master plan for stopping the
migration.

3
3. Petitioner further averred that people in the
hilly region depends upon its small agriculture which is
in danger due to wild animals, as between the villages
and forests areas, no strong boundaries are installed due
to which the wild animals, time and again, destroy the
agriculture crop and also cause harms to the human life,
as such a master plan is required for making strong
boundaries (through strong iron cables) between the
forest areas and the villages. Further, the State in these
sixteen years, after creation of the State, has almost
failed to promote Self Employment Schemes and
providing employment through small scale industries in
hilly region of the State. By establishing small scale
industries in the hilly regions such as plywood factories
(65% of the State is forest area) and other wooden based
small industries the State can provide employment to
the villagers of hilly region which would certainly help in
stopping migration, but it is highly shameful that State
has even did not think to create employment through
this type of small scale industries in the hilly region of
the State. In this regard, the petitioner's society moved a
detailed memorandum/representation, under signatures
of more than thousand of persons before the Hon'ble
Prime Minister through SDM Bhikiyasen District Almora,
in which several suggestion to prevent migration from
hilly region of the State have been given.
3. Petitioner further averred that in the
Uttarakhand State maximum population belongs to
remote/hilly region where the source of employment are
almost nil and women of these villages by doing petty
agriculture and dairy works are earning livelihood and a

4
big mass of males of the hilly and remote terrain of the
State has become habitual of alcohol and due to this evil
of alcohol, almost eighty percent of the families of the
hilly/remote region of the State, is suffering severe
hardships. In PIL Ravindra Jugran vs. State of
Uttarakhand, this Court has passed orders for
prohibiting the sale and purchase of liquor in three
districts of the State and the said order has been passed
on the basis of religious importance of the said three
districts. In this regard, it is stated that since the time of
the creation of new State of Uttarakhand and even prior
to the creation of the State, the public at large mainly
the women folk of the hilly region is agitating against the
sale of liquor in their areas. Time and again, the women
folk of the State have agitated against the sale of liquor
in their concern area and now this agitation has taken a
widest movement of the hilly districts of the State.
4. We have considered the submissions of
learned counsel for the petitioner and have also gone
through the entire material available on file.
5. So far as prayer no.1 seeking direction to the
respondents to prohibit sale and purchase of liquor in
the entire State of Uttarakhand on the basis of judgment
rendered by the Division Bench of this Court in Ravindra
Jugran's case is concerned, we have been informed that
the said judgment has been stayed by the Hon'ble Apex
Court. Besides this, we find that the petitioner has not
given any detail in the writ petition as to in what manner
liquor is badly affecting the life of people of the State.
Only copies of few newspaper items have been annexed,

5
in which ladies of the area are shown agitating against
the liquor shops. We further find that the liquor shops
are opened after sanction of valid license given by the
authority concerned; these shops are opened and run
after due permission from the competent authority. For
this purpose, policy is framed by the State Government.
Sale of liquor is not prohibited in State of Uttarakhand.
Unless, the said policy of the Government is challenged,
prayer for prohibiting sale and purchase of liquor cannot
be entertained.
6. As far as prayer of the petitioner for issuing a
mandamus to the respondents to prepare a master plan
for making strong boundaries (through strong iron
cables) between the forest areas and the villages of the
hilly regions of the State is concerned, we cannot
consider such prayer in absence of any detail in the
petition in regard thereto. The only thing which is
written in para-10 of the writ petition is that the
agriculture of the hilly areas of the State is in danger due
to wild animals as between the villages and forests areas
no strong boundaries have been installed due to which
the wild animals time and again destroy the agriculture
crops and also cause harm to the human life. We have
been told by the Government Counsel that this problem
is under consideration. Therefore, in absence of any
factual details, at this stage, we decline to pass any
order in this regard.
7. As regards the third prayer of the petitioner
for a direction to the respondents to provide adequate
facilities (including funds and infrastructure) to the

6
farmers of the hilly regions of State and to establish
small scale industries in the hilly regions such as
plywood factories (65% of the State is forest area) and
other wooden based small industries so that migration
be prevented from these village/hilly regions, the Court
finds that in this regard also, the writ petition is lacking
any details. It is informed by the State Counsel that
there are several schemes launched by the Central
Government and the State Government for the farmers/
unemployed youth for which loan/subsidies are given.
Needy can avail benefit of the same.
8. In view of the aforesaid discussion, no
direction can be issued to the respondents. The writ
petition is dismissed.

(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (V.K. Bist, J.)
 24.04.2017 24.04.2017
 Rajni
